source.text: days.pravoslavie.ru, 11 октября ст. ст. — «Мцц. Зинаиды и Филониллы (I).»
source.note: No rank is read onto her. Her line opens the day's second paragraph, which carries no icon; the day's two icons are both plain-service ones in the first paragraph, standing before the apostle Philip and before Theophanes of Nicaea.

attestations.note: The Russian adds two things the other two calendars did not give this folder: that the two women were kinswomen of the apostle Paul, and that they practised the art of medicine. Its index page heads her «Зинаида Тарсийская, мц.» and gives the healer's epithet to her sister rather than to her, «Филонилла Тарсийская, целительница» — so the `physician` type here is read off the life, which gives the medicine to both of them, and not off the index line. The «(I)» is the first century and no year is printed, so no `dates` are proposed.

source.text: doxologia.ro, calendarul zilei pentru 11 octombrie — «Sfânta Muceniță Zenaida»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 11ης Οκτωβρίου — «Αγίες Ζηναΐδα και Φιλονίλλα οι αδελφές»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 11 Οκτωβρίου εκάστου έτους», the same day the folder already keeps, and the entry is the same pair of sisters of Tarsus in Cilicia. The page argues against one piece of the tradition itself: some synaxaria say they were kinswomen of the Apostle Paul, but their names have nothing Hebrew about them and so, it says, that claim has no basis. It gives no year at all, so no `dates` object is proposed, and it adds the place of their death, a cave at Demetrias. It prints one apolytikion, which names them both and is taken here. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence on the life page.
Not checked: pravoslavno.rs for the corresponding Julian day (24 September 2026).

hymns.text: Τήν πολυθαύμαστον Ταρσόν τιμήσωμεν τήν ἐξανθήσασαν ἄνθη τά τίμια, τήν Ζηναΐδα τήν σοφήν καί Φιλονίλλαν. ἅμα δέ ἔχουσαι τῆς πίστεως τήν κρηπῖδα ἀσάλευτον, πᾶσαν τήν μυρίδα τῶν δαιμόνων κατήσχυναν. Διό καί σύν Ἀγγέλοις χορεύουσαι, ὑπέρ ἡμῶν ἀεί πρεσβεύουσιν.

source.text: saint.gr, Ἀπολυτίκιον, Ἦχος γ’ — the one hymn on the page of «Αγίες Ζηναΐδα και Φιλονίλλα οι αδελφές», and it names them both.

english.text: Let us honour much-wondered Tarsus, which brought to flower those precious blossoms, the wise Zenaida and Philonilla; for having together the foundation of the faith unshaken, they put to shame all the host of the demons. And so, dancing with the angels, they intercede for us always.
